The [[Lojban Creation Poem|Lojban Creation Poem]], though perilously obscure, is thought to embody some crucial aspects of '''[[lobykai|lobykai]]''' reality...

There is some carry-over from Loglan Mythology in Lojbanic Mythology, though it is not as widely known as it should be, and tends to be mentioned only by those old enough in the community to remember both. For example:

=== The four gods ===
Loglan has four gods:
*'''[[Jeeg|Jeeg]]''' and '''[[Talen|Talen]]''', who featured in an early Loglan [[Jeeg and Talen|anecdote]]
*'''[[The god R|The god R]]''', the Loglan equivalent of '''.y.''' (English ''er...'')
*'''Zipf''', after the formulator of [[Zipf's Law|Zipf's Law]]
===Other===
The history of Lojban is already becoming shrouded in myth. If Loglan is '''purjbo''', 'old-Lojban' (or in the gismu list, '''dzejbo''', 'elder Lojban'), the Lojban that existed prior to the Great Rafsi Shift of 7/93 is already partly unintelligible (including the poembook '''[[ziryroi|ziryroi]]''' by [[Michael Helsem|Michael Helsem]] (the word meant '''zirpu rokci''') - whose very title now means something different) &amp; must be considered '''mijyjbo''' ([[Middle Lojban]]). Here are some tales from '''lapoi pelxu ku'o trajynobli''' that pertain to the Loglan-Lojban split:
*[[In the Mountains|In the Mountains]]
*[[In the Pit #1]]
*[[In the Pit #2]]

There are also instances of mythos built up through metaphors bandied about on the [[Lojban mailing list|Lojban Mailing List]]:
*The [[Jimbob mythos]] was quite popular in the early 1990s.
*So was the [[ckafyzda Mythos|ckafyzda Mythos]], which motivated the first concerted effort in original Lojban writing.
